title: Pre-race examinations: What they are and how they work
covers: Pre-race veterinary examination; Lameness; Veterinary scratch
note: BHA explains regulatory pre-race examinations, gait/soundness checks, signs of lameness and withdrawal on veterinary grounds when concerns remain.

title: The role of the BHA in horse welfare
note: BHA states Veterinary Officers carry out pre-race checks and post-race checks after horses have run, with testing where appropriate.

title: HISA resources for veterinarians
covers: Pre-race examination; Post-race examination; Unsound; Veterinary inspection
note: HISA identifies pre-race, post-race and ad-hoc examinations as regulatory-veterinarian work and lists unsoundness/medical compromise among Veterinarians' List grounds.

title: HISA Issues Equine Health Advisory on the Veterinarians’ List
note: Current advisory reports horses classified Unsound by Regulatory Veterinarians and horses scratched by Regulatory Veterinarians; use as a US/HISA regulatory sense, not a universal synonym.

title: HISA ADMC Program in Full Swing Under HIWU
note: HIWU documents uniform sample collection by trained personnel and multiple official testing types under the ADMC Program.

title: The whip
note: BHA sets current limits and manner-of-use controls for the whip in Flat and Jump racing, with penalties for breaches.

title: HISA resources for racetrack personnel
note: HISA describes track-surface maintenance/testing, racetrack accreditation and safety-committee review of injuries, fatalities and other racetrack safety issues.

title: HISA Publishes 2026 Second Quarter Metrics Report
note: Current HISA metrics report racing/training-related equine fatalities, causes and horses with career-ending injuries who otherwise would have been euthanized; reporting definitions are program-specific.

title: Life after racing
note: BHA describes post-racing retirement pathways, retraining/rehoming and welfare-based euthanasia where responsible rehoming is not possible.

title: Racing Australia Annual Report 2025 — Welfare and Traceability
note: National reporting distinguishes retirement pathways/reasons, assisted rehoming, end-of-life outcomes and whether injuries occurred during work including race day.

title: Horse Welfare Committee and Principles of Good Practice
covers: Horse welfare; Injuries/fatalities; Emergency euthanasia; Aftercare; Whip
note: IFHA current Horse Welfare Committee material explicitly covers injury/fatality monitoring, emergency euthanasia on a racecourse, aftercare and use of the whip as welfare-practice areas.
